regulatory_status: routine clinical diagnostic; embedded in Lynch-syndrome screening and in tumour-agnostic checkpoint-inhibitor eligibility
interpretation: loss of nuclear staining in tumour with retained internal control = deficient MMR
pitfall: Heterodimer logic is mandatory: MSH6 loss can be secondary to MSH2 loss and PMS2 loss secondary to MLH1 loss. Scoring the four independently over-calls primary mutation. Prior chemoradiation and focal heterogeneous loss both cause false calls

targets: BAT-25 / BAT-26 / NR-21 / NR-24 / MONO-27 mononucleotide panel
interpretation: two or more unstable loci = MSI-high
pitfall: Minimal microsatellite shift occurs in MSI-high tumours - notably endometrial - and is a documented cause of false-negative interpretation. Requires matched normal and an analyst alert to small shifts

matrix: FFPE tumour or plasma cell-free DNA
regulatory_status: clinically deployed within comprehensive genomic profiling
interpretation: fraction of unstable loci above validated threshold
pitfall: Threshold is assay-specific and not transferable between callers. Low tumour fraction in plasma causes false negatives

regulatory_status: clinically used; predictive for alkylating chemotherapy benefit
interpretation: methylated promoter = silenced MGMT = retained alkylator sensitivity
pitfall: Cut-off definition between methylated and unmethylated is assay-dependent and the intermediate zone is genuinely ambiguous. Report the quantitative value not only the binary call

targets: loss of heterozygosity + telomeric allelic imbalance + large-scale state transitions
regulatory_status: clinically deployed as a companion-style biomarker for PARP-inhibitor decisions
interpretation: composite genomic-scar score above threshold = HR deficient
pitfall: A genomic scar is a historical record; it does not report present-day HR function. Must be read alongside the RAD51 functional read-out to avoid misclassifying a reverted; resistant tumour as HR deficient
Variants of uncertain significance are common and are not actionable. Large rearrangements require dedicated copy-number analysis
A consequence of accumulated repair failure rather than a repair measurement. Mechanistically uninformative on its own - always interpret against the mutational-signature result

interpretation: signature weights attributable to MMR deficiency; HR deficiency; oxidative damage; alkylation
pitfall: Requires adequate mutation count; exome-scale data give unstable signature fits. This is the only element that assigns observed mutations to a specific failed pathway
